questions.prompt: Which control surfaces roll the aircraft around its longitudinal axis?
questions.explanation: Ailerons on the outer trailing edge of each wing move in opposite directions, raising one wing and lowering the other.

questions.prompt: Moving the elevator rotates the aircraft around which axis?
questions.explanation: The lateral axis runs wingtip to wingtip. The elevator pitches the nose up or down around it.

questions.prompt: The rudder controls movement around which axis?
questions.explanation: The rudder swings the nose left or right, which is yaw around the vertical axis.

questions.prompt: What are the four forces acting on an aircraft in flight?
questions.explanation: Lift opposes weight, and thrust opposes drag. In steady, level flight they balance.

questions.prompt: Angle of attack is the angle between the wing's chord line and the
choices: flight path of the previous aircraft
questions.explanation: Angle of attack is measured against the oncoming airflow. The angle between the chord line and the fuselage is the angle of incidence, a different thing.

questions.prompt: A wing stalls when
choices: it exceeds its critical angle of attack
questions.explanation: A stall is caused by too high an angle of attack, which disrupts smooth airflow over the wing. It can happen at any airspeed or attitude.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of wing flaps?
choices: To add lift and drag for slower, steeper approaches
questions.explanation: Flaps change the wing's shape, so it makes more lift at low speed. The added drag also allows a steeper descent without gaining speed.

questions.prompt: In a level turn with a 60-degree bank, the load factor is about
questions.explanation: Load factor in a level turn is 1 divided by the cosine of the bank angle. The cosine of 60 degrees is 0.5, so 1 / 0.5 = 2 G.

questions.prompt: Ground effect, felt within about one wingspan of the ground, mainly reduces
questions.explanation: The ground interferes with the wingtip vortices, reducing induced drag. That's why airplanes tend to float just before touchdown.

questions.prompt: Runway 27 is lined up with a magnetic heading of about
questions.explanation: Runway numbers are the magnetic heading divided by 10 and rounded: 270 degrees becomes 27.

questions.prompt: What number is painted on the opposite end of Runway 09?
questions.explanation: The two ends of a runway differ by 180 degrees: 090 + 180 = 270, so the other end is Runway 27.

questions.prompt: What color are taxiway edge lights?
questions.explanation: Taxiway edges are blue. Runway edges are white, and taxiway centerline lights are green.

questions.prompt: What color are runway edge lights along most of the runway?
questions.explanation: Runway edge lights are white. On instrument runways, the last 2,000 feet show yellow as a caution zone.

questions.prompt: To a pilot about to land, the runway threshold lights appear
questions.explanation: Threshold lights show green toward approaching aircraft and red toward aircraft on the runway, marking the runway's end.

questions.prompt: On a PAPI, two white lights and two red lights mean the aircraft is
questions.explanation: A PAPI uses four lights. Two white and two red means on glide path, more white means high, and more red means low.

questions.prompt: On a PAPI, four white lights mean the aircraft is
choices: lined up with the wrong runway
questions.explanation: All white means too high. All red means dangerously low.

questions.prompt: A rotating beacon flashing white and green marks a
questions.explanation: White and green is a civilian land airport. White and yellow marks a water airport, and a military airport shows two quick white flashes between each green.

questions.prompt: An altimeter finds altitude by measuring
questions.explanation: Air pressure drops as you climb. A standard altimeter converts static pressure to altitude.

questions.prompt: An airspeed indicator works by comparing
choices: the compass heading with the wind
questions.explanation: The faster the airplane moves, the more ram pressure enters the pitot tube compared with the still air at the static port.

questions.prompt: The vertical speed indicator shows
choices: the rate of climb or descent
questions.explanation: It reads in feet per minute, positive in a climb and negative in a descent.

questions.prompt: The attitude indicator shows the aircraft's
choices: pitch and bank relative to the horizon
questions.explanation: Its miniature airplane and horizon bar show whether the nose is up or down and whether the wings are banked.

questions.prompt: Why must the heading indicator be checked against the magnetic compass during flight?
choices: It shows true north instead of magnetic
It only works on the ground
It runs on a battery that fades
questions.explanation: Friction makes the gyroscope precess, so pilots reset the heading indicator to the compass every 15 minutes or so in steady flight.

questions.prompt: In a coordinated turn, the ball in the turn coordinator is
choices: toward the inside of the turn
at the top of its tube
toward the outside of the turn
questions.explanation: A centered ball means no slip or skid. Pilots "step on the ball" with rudder to center it.

questions.prompt: A knot is a speed of one
questions.explanation: A nautical mile is about 6,076 feet, so 1 knot is about 1.15 miles per hour.

questions.prompt: Mach 1 is
choices: the speed needed to reach orbit
questions.explanation: The speed of sound changes with air temperature, so Mach 1 is slower at high, cold altitudes than at sea level.

questions.prompt: Which condition increases density altitude and reduces aircraft performance?
questions.explanation: Heat, height, and humidity all thin the air. Thinner air means less lift and less engine power.

questions.prompt: Taking off into a headwind
choices: has no effect on the takeoff roll
questions.explanation: The wing needs a certain airspeed. A headwind supplies some of it, so the airplane reaches flying speed at a lower groundspeed.

questions.prompt: Adverse yaw, the nose swinging away from a turn when the ailerons are used, is corrected with the
questions.explanation: The rising wing has more drag and pulls the nose the wrong way. Rudder in the direction of the turn cancels it.

questions.prompt: What do trim tabs do?
choices: Relieve the pilot from holding steady control pressure
Steer the aircraft on the ground
questions.explanation: Trim holds a control surface in position, so the pilot doesn't have to keep pushing or pulling.

questions.prompt: In a helicopter, the collective control
choices: tilts the rotor disc forward or sideways
steers the helicopter on the ground
changes the pitch of all main rotor blades at once
questions.explanation: Raising the collective increases every blade's pitch together, so the helicopter climbs. Tilting the disc is the cyclic's job.

questions.prompt: A helicopter's cyclic control
choices: locks the rotor on the ground
tilts the main rotor disc to move forward, back, or sideways
changes the pitch of all blades at once
questions.explanation: Tilting the rotor disc tilts its lift, pulling the helicopter in that direction.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of a helicopter's tail rotor?
choices: To provide a backup power source
To counteract the torque of the main rotor
questions.explanation: As the main rotor turns one way, the body tries to spin the other way. The tail rotor pushes against that, and the pedals adjust it to control yaw.

questions.prompt: Autorotation lets a helicopter
choices: descend under control after an engine failure
questions.explanation: Air flowing up through the rotor as the helicopter descends keeps the blades turning, so the pilot can still steer and flare for landing.

questions.prompt: In the phonetic alphabet, the letter T is
questions.explanation: Pilots use Alfa, Bravo, Charlie... Tango. Tare was used in an older alphabet that is no longer used.

questions.prompt: In military time, 2:30 p.m. is written
questions.explanation: Add 12 to afternoon hours: 2 + 12 = 14, so 1430.

questions.prompt: A pilot sets the transponder to 7700 to signal
questions.explanation: 7700 means emergency, 7600 means lost communications, and 7500 means hijacking.

questions.prompt: What does transponder code 7600 mean?
choices: The aircraft is a military jet
The aircraft has lost radio communication
questions.explanation: 7600 tells controllers the pilot can't talk to them, so they clear the way and expect standard lost-communication procedures.

questions.prompt: According to Bernoulli's principle, as air speeds up over the top of a wing, its pressure
questions.explanation: Faster-moving air has lower pressure. Lower pressure above the wing and higher pressure below help create lift.

questions.prompt: Induced drag is greatest when the aircraft is
choices: flying slowly at a high angle of attack
questions.explanation: Induced drag comes from making lift. It is highest at low speed, when the wing works hardest. Parasite drag is the type that grows with speed.

questions.prompt: The curve of a wing's airfoil from front to back is called
questions.explanation: Camber is the curve of the airfoil. The chord is the straight line from leading edge to trailing edge.

questions.prompt: Dihedral, the upward angle of the wings from root to tip, improves
questions.explanation: With dihedral, a wing that dips gains lift and helps level the airplane on its own.

questions.prompt: A center of gravity that is too far aft makes an airplane
choices: less stable and harder to recover from a stall
questions.explanation: The tail has less leverage to keep the nose under control, so the airplane becomes unstable and may not recover from a stall.

questions.prompt: At a runway holding position marking, an aircraft waiting for clearance stays on the side with the
questions.explanation: The marking has two solid and two dashed yellow lines. Stop on the solid side until cleared onto the runway.

questions.prompt: The runway area before a displaced threshold, marked with white arrows, may be used for
choices: takeoff and landing rollout, but not touchdown
questions.explanation: You may take off from it or roll through it after landing, but you must touch down past the threshold line.
